                    ### Question
                    A 55-year-old Caucasian male presents for a routine colonoscopy. A polyp is found in the patient's transverse colon and is found to be cancerous on histological evaluation. Upon examination, it is found that these cancerous cells have decreased MHC class I expression on their surface. Which immune system cell is most capable of killing these tumor cells?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Natural killer cells
opb. B-cells
opc. Macrophages
opd. Eosinophils
ope. Cytotoxic T-cells

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Natural killer (NK) cells are the most capable immune cells for killing tumor cells with decreased MHC class I expression, as they utilize 'missing self' recognition to detect and eliminate such cells. This mechanism compensates for the reduced effectiveness of cytotoxic T-cells under these conditions. Evidence supports NK cells' interaction with both the Major Histocompatibility Complex and unspecified tumor cells, confirming their pivotal role in targeting cells that evade typical immune surveillance by downregulating MHC class I.
